judged_text: Blacklisted emails are silently filtered out of the guest list while the handler still returns success. An operator maintaining BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS gets no signal, and the acting user sees the 'Guests added' toast while the blacklisted address was never added — a silent partial application of the requested action.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler`, the input `guests` is filtered into `uniqueGuests` by removing already-attending emails and any in `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` (see `uniqueGuests = guests.filter(... && !blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest))`). The mutation proceeds and returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` as long as `uniqueGuests.length !== 0`, even if some requested emails were blacklisted and therefore not added. On the client, `onSuccess` always shows `showToast(t("guests_added"), "success")`, so the acting user receives a full-success toast despite partial application, and there is no logging/notification about blacklisted emails being ignored (only a generic email-send catch log).
